title: ClearHead Transaction Request
description: A batch of semantic action operations that must validate together and commit together through one PendingBatch. Operations are applied in array order against trusted workspace state loaded under the workspace lock; any invalid operation rejects the whole batch before a write. This is NOT a JSON Patch or a desired-state document: each operation names an intent (update / complete / cancel / reopen) whose in-place field and date changes core owns. Complete, cancel, and reopen affect only the named action: no cascade, no parent-link detachment, and no file move. Single-item work should use the ordinary verbs; a transaction exists only for edits that must be atomic together. Dry-run is an invocation flag (`clearhead transact --dry-run`), not part of this document.

operations.description: Ordered operations. Applied in sequence; the batch is all-or-nothing.

canonicalId.description: Canonical action identity as a urn:uuid IRI, the exact spelling the query contract exports and the CLI resolver accepts.

updateAction.description: Edit an open action's attributes in place (single file). Core refuses a closed target altogether, even when no state edit is requested. No cascade, no move. State may be set to a NON-terminal value here; terminal transitions (completed / cancelled) are rejected by core in favor of complete-action / cancel-action, which stamp state and completed_at together. Use reopen-action to reopen a closed action and clear its completed_at.

set.description: Fields to change; mirrors core's ActionUpdate applier surface. At least one field. Dependency-graph edits (predecessors, is_sequential) are intentionally out of the v1 operation set.

context.description: Context tags as bare names (no leading '+'). Replaces the existing set.

state.description: Action state, serialized as core ActionState does (snake_case; BlockedOrAwaiting => 'blocked'). Terminal values 'completed'/'cancelled' are accepted structurally but rejected by core's terminal-state guard — use complete-action / cancel-action instead. To reopen a closed action, use reopen-action rather than a field update.

scheduled_at.description: The do-date, written as '@' takes it: an ISO 8601 date or date-time (the planned start), or a start/end interval (a planned block), e.g. 2026-04-01T09:00/2026-04-01T09:30. Duration is the block's length (Decision 51).

completeAction.description: Close only the named action in place: set state to completed and stamp completed_at. No cascade, no parent-link detachment, and no file move. Descendants and the action's parent link are unchanged; closed lines remain ordinary records in the active file. Archival is a separate whole-root-tree operation.

cancelAction.description: Cancel only the named action in place: set state to cancelled and stamp completed_at. No cascade, no parent-link detachment, and no file move. Descendants and the action's parent link are unchanged; archival is a separate whole-root-tree operation.

reopenAction.description: Reopen only the named closed action in place: set state to not_started and clear completed_at. Allowed only in the active file; refused if archived (unarchive its root tree first). No cascade, no parent-link detachment, and no file move. Descendants and the action's parent link are unchanged.
